chunks: Muhammad ibn Ali Majilawayh narrated from his uncle Muhammad ibn Abi al-Qasim, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from al-Husayn ibn Sa'id al-Azraq, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him)
In the case of a man who killed a believing man, it is said to him: 'Die whichever death you wish: if you wish, die a Jew; if you wish, die a Christian; if you wish, die a Magian.'
ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on the death of a person who kills a believer according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: In this narration from Shaykh al-Saduq, Imam Ja'far al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) elucidates the specific legal consequence for one who kills a believer, denying them the natural option of dying as a Muslim. Instead, the killer is granted the choice to die as a Jew, Christian, or Magian, a ruling that highlights the unique status of the victim's faith and the distinct spiritual penalty borne by the murderer. This emphasizes the gravity of *qatl al-nafs* in Shia jurisprudence, where the killer's soul is separated from the fold of Islam in a manner distinct from general apostasy.
